summary: AI observability has become essential in 2026 as LLM-powered applications scale into production, with New Relic reporting 30% quarter-over-quarter growth in AI monitoring adoption. These tools capture the trace behind each production outcome—prompts, responses, retrieval context, model calls, costs, and quality scores—helping teams detect hallucinations, control spend, and debug failures that traditional APM cannot explain. Choosing the right tool depends on your framework, self-hosting needs, and whether your priority is deep evaluation or lightweight cost governance.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: Prompts, traces, token usage, latency, cost breakdowns, and evaluation metrics—especially deep, zero-config tracing for LangChain and LangGraph applications.
features: Detailed cost and token breakdowns per trace
tools.pricing: Seat-based plus usage; starts around $39/user/month. Per-trace overage charges can add roughly 5–10% of underlying LLM API spend for trace-heavy workloads.
tools.best_for: Teams whose architecture is built on LangChain or LangGraph and want deep, out-of-the-box tracing that justifies vendor coupling.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API costs, request volume, latency, and per-user/per-department spend via a lightweight proxy gateway.
features: Single-line base URL change for integration (under 5 minutes)
tools.pricing: Request-based pricing with a generous free tier; self-hostable for free and charges zero markup on LLM costs.
tools.best_for: Teams who want instant, low-overhead visibility into LLM spend and fast cost governance without framework coupling.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B Weave)
tools.monitors: Model experiments, LLM application traces, evaluations, prompt performance, and data quality across the ML/LLM lifecycle.
features: Weave for LLM tracing and evaluation
tools.pricing: Free tier for individuals; team and enterprise plans are usage- and seat-based with custom enterprise pricing.
tools.best_for: ML teams who already use W&B for experiment tracking and want unified observability spanning training and LLM production.

tools.name: Arize AI (Phoenix)
tools.monitors: Model performance, data quality, embeddings/drift, retrieval quality, and LLM evaluation with OpenTelemetry-based tracing.
tools.pricing: Phoenix is open-source and free to self-host; Arize AX enterprise platform uses usage-based/custom pricing.
tools.best_for: Teams prioritizing deep evaluation, drift detection, and open-standard (OpenTelemetry) observability with self-hosting flexibility.

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: Traces, spans, prompts, token usage, costs, latency, and evaluation scores across multiple frameworks.
features: Cost and token tracking per trace
tools.pricing: Open-source with free self-hosting; managed cloud offers a free tier plus usage-based paid plans.
tools.best_for: Teams needing self-hosting, data ownership, and multi-framework support as a flexible, cost-controlled alternative to LangSmith.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM calls, traces, token usage, and latency using OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation that exports to any compatible backend.
features: Integrates with Datadog, New Relic, Grafana, etc.
tools.pricing: Free and open-source; costs are only those of the backend you export telemetry to.
tools.best_for: Engineering teams who want standards-based, vendor-neutral LLM telemetry piped into their existing observability stack.

cost_tips: Use a lightweight gateway/proxy like Helicone or Portkey with zero markup to track per-user and per-department spend, then enable response caching to avoid paying for repeated identical queries.
Route requests to the cheapest model that meets quality requirements—reserve frontier models for complex tasks and use smaller/cheaper models for routine or classification work.
Trim token usage by shortening prompts, compressing retrieval context, setting sensible max_output_token limits, and removing redundant system instructions.

Watch trace-heavy observability overhead: per-trace charges (e.g., LangSmith's ~5–10% of LLM spend) can add up, so consider sampling traces or self-hosting open-source tools like Langfuse or Phoenix for high-volume workloads.
